title: Steam-First Reverse Sear for Brussels Sprouts, Cabbage, and Fennel
summary: The video demonstrates a vegetable reverse-sear workflow adapted from meat cookery: trim and shape Brussels sprouts, cabbage, and fennel into flat, uniform pieces; cook the interior with steam before exposing the surface to high heat for browning. The prep emphasizes flat sides and even sizing to maximize pan contact, while the technique employs water-based steaming (with optional brine) to deliver heat to interior portions. After steaming, the lid/foil is removed to allow Maillard browning, aided by oil to improve heat transfer. The segment concludes with plating ideas (maple vinaigrette, smoked almonds, sesame seeds, scallions) and notes on applying this method to other vegetables like cauliflower and broccoli.
